title: Ulyana and the Atlas
premise: In the port city of Vellamare, 1789, apprentice mapmaker Casper Ravensworth inherits the unfinished atlas of their dead master, Aldous Wren — an atlas whose final charts trace the coastline of a nation now declared enemy. When a census taker discovers that Casper has been hiding the identity of their late master's correspondent, Ilse Marchetti, a cartographer on the wrong side of the border, Casper becomes both suspect and asset to a government that wants the atlas's secrets and a family that wants its truth. To honor a promise made in peacetime — that the atlas would reach Ilse's hands — Casper must smuggle the completed charts aboard a departing ship while dodging the census officer turned inquisitor, learning along the way that the family they found in Wren's workshop was never theirs alone. The atlas sails at dawn; Casper, spared by an unexpected act of mercy from the inquisitor who once loved Wren too, stays behind to keep the workshop — and its found family — alive.
about_author: Emrys Hartwell is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing maritime charts and the letters folded inside them. Hartwell writes historical fiction about the quiet keepers of knowledge, and lives near a harbor where the tide still keeps better time than any clock.

chapters.title: The Ink That Would Not Dry
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Three months after Master Wren's death, Casper keeps the workshop running, finishing the atlas plate by plate while pretending nothing is unfinished in their own grief. They discover a sealed letter addressed to Ilse Marchetti in enemy territory. Beat: quiet devotion masking fear that the promise cannot be kept.

chapters.title: A Question of Residence
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. The annual census arrives; the taker, Mr. Quill, is unusually thorough, asking who taught Casper, who corresponded with Wren, and whether any 'foreign persons' are owed debts by the estate. Casper lies badly. Beat: the first crack in the safe little life.

chapters.title: The Widow Next Door
chapters.summary: Marta, the workshop's elderly colorist, POV. Marta reveals she knew about Ilse all along — Wren's letters passed through her hands for years. She warns Casper that Quill once worked for the Admiralty and doesn't ask questions for curiosity's sake. Beat: found family deepens; the secret becomes shared weight.

chapters.title: Charts of a Forbidden Coast
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Casper studies Wren's final plates and realizes the atlas isn't just beautiful — it's strategically valuable, mapping harbors the navy doesn't know. That's why Wren was traveling when he died. Beat: awe curdling into dread; the atlas is a weapon whether Casper wants it to be or not.

chapters.title: The Second Visit
chapters.summary: Quill's POV. Quill returns with a warrant to 'inventory' the workshop's papers. He finds the letter to Ilse but, strangely, leaves it — and leaves a card with an address. Casper realizes he wants something more than arrest. Beat: the antagonist becomes ambiguous; menace with a human face.

chapters.title: Letters in a Dead Man's Hand
chapters.summary: Casper's POV, interleaved with Wren's letters read aloud. The letters reveal Wren and Ilse were rivals, then collaborators, then something like family — and that Wren promised her the atlas would be hers. Casper understands the promise is not optional. Beat: inheritance redefined as obligation and love.

chapters.title: The Harbormaster's Daughter
chapters.summary: New character Sefa, a young harbor worker, POV. Sefa owes Marta a debt and agrees to learn which ships sail on the morning tides. She and Casper begin an uneasy friendship over shared maps of the harbor. Beat: the circle of allies widens; hope with practical hands.

chapters.title: Inventory
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Government clerks seal the workshop's map room. Casper hides the finished atlas plates inside a commissioned family portrait's backing, working nights. Marta's hands shake painting the border. Beat: claustrophobic tension; art as concealment, family as conspiracy.

chapters.title: What Quill Wants
chapters.summary: Quill's POV. Flashback to Quill and Wren's shared youth in the survey corps, and the falling-out when Wren chose Ilse's coast over the Crown's. Quill doesn't want the atlas destroyed; he wants to finish it, as Wren's true heir. Beat: the antagonist's grief mirrors Casper's; two heirs, one atlas.

chapters.title: The Summons
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Casper is summoned to the Admiralty and offered a bargain: complete the atlas for the navy, and the letter — and Casper's freedom — are forfeit. Refusal means charges of harboring enemy correspondence. Beat: the trap closes; Casper buys three days by claiming the atlas needs one final plate.

chapters.title: Three Days
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV rotation — Marta, Sefa, Casper. The workshop becomes a machine of quiet resistance: Marta forges a shipping manifest, Sefa secures passage on the Meridian, Casper inks the final plate by candlelight. Beat: found family in full motion, each member risking what they can afford to lose.

chapters.title: The Plate That Lies
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. To buy time, Casper gives the Admiralty a deliberately flawed proof — one harbor drawn a cable's length wrong. Quill, examining it, hesitates: he recognizes Wren's technique and knows the error is deliberate. He says nothing. Beat: complicity; the antagonist's first betrayal of his own side.

chapters.title: Marta's Confession
chapters.summary: Marta's POV. Marta admits she was once Ilse's teacher, that the three of them — Wren, Ilse, Marta — were a family of maps before Casper was born, and that she stayed silent for years out of cowardice. She gives Casper Ilse's last known address. Beat: generational guilt and grace; the promise passes down a chain of hands.

chapters.title: The Tailor's Shop
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Casper scouts the Meridian's captain, a smuggler of silk who owes Wren an old favor, and negotiates passage for a 'roll of carpets.' The captain's price: the atlas's northern plate, a copy Casper refuses to give. Negotiation stalls. Beat: hope priced beyond comfort.

chapters.title: Quill's Choice
chapters.summary: Quill's POV. Quill's superiors grow suspicious of his slow inventory; he is ordered to arrest the apprentice at dawn. Alone with Wren's old compass, Quill decides which heir Wren would have chosen — or decides to make the choice himself, once and for all. Beat: the antagonist turns; the climax is set in motion.

chapters.title: Night Tide
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. The smuggling goes wrong: a clerk, not Quill, ambushes the workshop. Marta stalls him with forged papers while Casper flees across rooftops with the atlas wrapped in sailcloth. Sefa is caught and won't give a name. Beat: full panic; the family's sacrifice made visible.

chapters.title: The Weighing of Anchors
chapters.summary: Casper's POV, pre-dawn. Quill intercepts Casper at the quay — not to arrest, but to carry one end of the atlas. He gives Casper the letter, stamped with official seals to pass inspection: his final forgery, his inheritance refused. Beat: climax of grace; enemy becomes executor of the promise.

chapters.title: Morning Tide
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. The Meridian sails with the atlas and the letter aboard. Casper stands on the quay as the coast that killed their master slides out of sight, keeping its secrets. Sefa, released for lack of evidence, joins them. Beat: release and grief braided together; the promise kept at cost.

chapters.title: What the Census Found
chapters.summary: Quill's POV. Quill files his report: workshop cleared, no enemy correspondence found, one apprentice of good character. He keeps only one thing — a single unfinished sketch of the three cartographers, Wren, Ilse, and Marta, young together. Beat: quiet absolution; the record falsified into mercy.

chapters.title: The Empty Chair
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. The workshop reopens. Casper takes Wren's chair, hires Sefa as an apprentice, and begins a new atlas — of Vellamare itself, its harbors and its people, no state's name on the title page. Beat: grief transmuted into vocation; identity chosen, not assigned.

chapters.title: A Letter Comes
chapters.summary: Casper's POV, months later. A letter arrives, postmarked from across the border, in a hand Casper knows only from Wren's descriptions: Ilse's. She has the atlas. She writes one sentence: 'Tell whoever kept the promise that they are family, and family is owed a visit.' Beat: the found family completes its circle across a border.

chapters.title: The Atlas of Small Things
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. Spring. Marta teaches Sefa to mix vermilion, Quill visits on his day off and pretends to inspect the premises, and Casper inks the first plate of the new atlas — a map of the workshop itself, every chair and hand that made it home. Beat: resolution; memory and identity settled into place, the tide coming in on time.
